title: Triangle decompositions of dense tripartite graphs and completion of partial Latin squares
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Corollary 1.6 for r = 3 of Barber, Kühn, Lo, Osthus and Taylor, "Clique decompositions of multipartite graphs and completion of Latin squares" (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 151 (2017), arXiv:1603.01043): fractional triangle decompositions above a threshold give triangle decompositions above the same threshold. Precisely: if δ ≥ 3/4 and, for every ε > 0, every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with three parts of size n ≥ n₀(ε) and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a fractional triangle decomposition, then for every ε > 0 there is n₀ such that every K₃-divisible tripartite graph with parts of size n ≥ n₀ and minimum partite degree at least (δ + ε)n has a triangle decomposition (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6). The hypothesis δ ≥ 3/4 is an extra assumption of the Lean statement: the article does not need it because the fractional threshold is known to be at least 3/4, which is not formalized here. Combined with the fractional bound of Allsop, Bowtell, Lesgourgues and Petrova (pinned entry PALOMAR-2026-10-30-000008), this gives the unconditional statement with threshold 0.769 − 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.corollary_1_6_ablp). The proof follows the iterative absorption of the article (absorbers, vortex of partitions with random reserves, cover-down, balancing graph, assembly) but replaces the regularity-based Section 8 by a route through the fractional threshold and the Haxell–Rödl transfer. Version 2 adds Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 3.2 for r = 3, the completion of partial Latin squares: for every ε > 0 and all large n, every partial Latin square of order n in which every row, every column and every symbol is used at most (1 − δ − ε)n times extends to a Latin square, above the fractional threshold δ ≥ 3/4 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4, from Cor16 δ by BKLOT2017.corollary_3_2) and unconditionally with 1 − δ = 0.231 + 1/20000 (BKLOT2017.theorem_1_4_ablp).
